notes:
Summary: Crestline is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for an enterprise-grade, low-latency personalization/chat stack across payments and account ops. Primary ask: predictable throughput (QPS) and hard latency SLOs for high-value flows. They are cost-conscious but prioritize reliability for peak traffic windows.

What they told us / key constraints:
- "We need 99th percentile latency under 120ms for payment-related chat transactions during peak hours." (product lead)
- Peak traffic pattern: bursty (30–45 min peaks) around batch settlement times; expected steady-state QPS ~120 QPS for chat, peak bursts up to 600 QPS for short periods.
- Token profile: median response ~120 tokens, worst-case up to 1.2k tokens (document summarization fallback).
- Hard requirement: VPC + customer-managed KMS; audit logs retention 7 years for specific flows.
- Prefer reserved GPU pools (predictable throughput) but want automated burst policy for rare peaks.

Sizing workshop scope (proposed):
- Week 1: Telemetry collection + synthetic replay of 2-week traffic (we provide harness + Crestline provides logs). Establish baseline QPS and token/sec distributions.
- Week 2: Dedicated sizing run (staged): run on 1/4 capacity, iterate batching/quantization settings, measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token/sec. Validate autoscale/burst policy. Deliver recommended reserved GPU count and backup routing policies.

POC / SLA asks to address in workshop + contract:
- Throughput guarantees: target sustained throughput per reserved GPU and documented fallback when saturated.
- Latency SLOs: p99 < 120ms for payment chat flows at agreed load; p99 for large summarization flows TBD.
- SLA credits model for missed SLOs and clear escalation path to Ops.

Open action items / blockers:
- Infosec wants SOC2 Type II + ISO27001 proof before test env access (ACTIONS: Amanda to send certs).
- Crestline needs detailed GPU sizing + cost delta for burst capacity vs higher reservation. Finance wants a 3-year TCO comparison (on-prem vs Redwood Dedicated).
- Need to confirm data residency mapping for EU customers; legal to review data processing addendum.

- "If you can prove 99p under load, procurement is comfortable with a 2-year commit." — Finance director
